primary_source.content: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav said the Centre and state are jointly accelerating Madhya Pradesh’s development through major industrial and infrastructure initiatives. He said addressing the Viksit Bharat Industry and Trade Summit in Bhopal, that investment proposals worth ₹12 lakh crore had been translated into projects on the ground over the past two-and-a-half years, while entrepreneurs at the summit proposed fresh investments worth ₹7,500 crore.Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that investment proposals worth ₹12 lakh crore had been translated into projects on the ground in the state over the past two-and-a-half years. Madhya Pradesh is strengthening its position across sectors, and transparent policies have made it easier for investors to establish industries. Investment promotion programmes and activities are being organised regularly to generate employment for the youth.Industry Brings Prosperity to PeopleChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that entrepreneurs contribute to improving people’s lives through investment across sectors. Their efforts in trade and industry sustain the livelihoods of millions of families. He also commended the industry’s active role in advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Make in India vision.Global Recognition for IndiaChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, major countries around the world have begun viewing India with greater respect. He emphasised that Madhya Pradesh has considerable potential and that greater focus is needed on economic prosperity alongside agricultural development.Other States Adopting Madhya Pradesh’s Industrial ModelChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that Bhopal is hosting the Global Investors Summit for the second time, reflecting the state’s efforts to create an industry-friendly environment. The Regional Industry Conclave model developed by Madhya Pradesh has been appreciated by other states, several of which are adopting it. He said the Bhoomi Poojan performed earlier by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for the ₹50,000-crore downstream petrochemical unit at Bina Refinery would enable production of more than 2.2 million tonnes of petrochemical products annually in the coming years. These developments will accelerate growth not only in Madhya Pradesh but across the country.Chief Minister Dr. Yadav also released several publications brought out by the Federation. MSME Minister Shri Chaitanya Kashyap said the Chief Minister had helped create a favourable environment for investment in Madhya Pradesh. Hundreds of entrepreneurs associated with around a dozen federations are participating in the two-day summit. He highlighted initiatives such as the Regional Development Plan and metropolitan areas, noting that these had strengthened confidence in the state’s industry and trade sectors.

Oil prices rise more than 1% as supply concerns linger - Reuters

brief_bullets: Gold prices are tracking toward a significant weekly decline as surging oil prices exacerbate inflationary pressures, complicating the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy outlook. Crude oil futures climbed over 1% amid persistent global supply concerns, prompting investors to reassess the likelihood of sustained high interest rates. As yields on government bonds rise in response to these inflationary signals, non-yielding assets like gold have faced substantial selling pressure. This market shift reflects a broader investor pivot toward hedging against prolonged restrictive policy, as the intersection of energy volatility and central bank hawkishness diminishes the appeal of precious metals. Consequently, gold remains vulnerable to further downward momentum as traders await clearer signals regarding the Federal Reserve's future interest rate trajectory.
why_it_matters_bullets: Rising energy costs threaten to keep inflation elevated, forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive rates, pressuring non-yielding assets.

primary_source.headline: Pete Ricketts’s Wealth Puts Class at the Center of Nebraska’s Senate Race
primary_source.content: In a year when the wealth of the rich soared while workers lost ground to inflation, class has become political, especially in the Nebraska Senate race.

sources.headline: Pete Ricketts’s Wealth Puts Class at the Center of Nebraska’s Senate Race
Chris Pappas Could Make History in New Hampshire’s Senate Race

brief_bullets: Nebraska’s Senate race has evolved into a sharp referendum on economic inequality as incumbent Pete Ricketts faces scrutiny over his substantial personal wealth. Amidst a national climate where inflationary pressures have eroded the purchasing power of average workers, Ricketts’s financial background has become a central point of contention for his political opponents. This dynamic highlights a broader trend in American politics where candidates’ socioeconomic status increasingly dictates voter perception and campaign messaging. While Ricketts leverages his business experience, critics argue his immense fortune creates a disconnect from the daily struggles of middle-class Nebraskans, effectively transforming the contest into a high-stakes debate over class representation and the influence of elite wealth in the legislative process.
why_it_matters_bullets: The focus on Ricketts’s wealth underscores how economic disparity is reshaping electoral strategies and voter alignment in modern politics.

primary_source.headline: SBI customers’ data leak: Here’s how to protect yourself from phishing attacks
primary_source.content: Earlier this week, a report emerged that the customer database server of the State Bank of India was breached. And, customer data was being sold on darknet for the highest bidder.The exposed information includes account owners' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers (customer information file number), lead IDs (unique reference number generated to track a potential customer), and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsSBI customers’ data leak: Here’s how to protect yourself from phishing attacksIn one lineFollowing a data breach exposing State Bank of India customer records, experts urge users to follow strict cybersecurity practices against phishing.Step-by-step1Stay calm during intimidating callsIf you receive alarming calls from individuals posing as officials threatening account seizure, do not panic. Cut the call and verify directly at your nearest bank branch.2Secure your login credentialsRegularly update your netbanking passwords across both web and mobile applications to prevent unauthorized access.3Avoid suspicious links and APKsNever click on URL links or install APK files shared via WhatsApp, messengers, or social media, as they frequently contain malware.4Download apps from official storesEnsure you only install applications from recognized platforms like the Google Play Store, Apple App Store, or Microsoft Windows Store after checking user reviews.5Keep devices updated and protectedMaintain fully updated operating systems with the latest security patches and install reputable anti-virus software to defend against cyber threats.Key statistics4,000Reported affected accounts99 per centRisk rate of unverified APK files1930Emergency fraud helplineOne hourTime limit to report fraud for best recovery chanceProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Though it claims there is leakage of customer data of close to 4,000 accounts, the exposure seems much bigger.And, SBI's customers are still at risk of getting scammed online, particularly through frauds like phishing attacks and digital arrest.Google rolls out new AI-powered security features to Chrome to curb online fraudIt should be noted that the highest bidder on the darknet may now have thousands of customers' data with personally identifiable credentials. With that, they disguise themselves as a bank executive, CBI officer, an Income Tax official or a Supreme Court/High Court judge, and will surely make calls to customers of the leaked data.Here are tips on how to safeguard yourself from online scams like phishing and digital arrests:1) Whenever you receive a call from a person identifying themselves as a police or Income Tax official, a cellular company executive or a bank official stating that your account may get seized, never panic. Just tell them, I will speak to a bank official and just cut the call. Go to the nearest bank branch and clear the doubt.2) Regularly change the password of your netbanking account, both on the website and on the phone app.3)  If you ever receive messages with URL links to third-party app stores or APK files resembling a bank app, ignore them. Never install an APK file shared on WhatsApp or any messenger or social media platform. For 99 per cent of the time, they are risky and potentially come with malware-laced files.4) Always install and download apps from the official Google Play Store, Microsoft Windows Store, and Apple App Store only.Supreme Court cautions of fake website created for phishing attack, stealing user details5) Even if you are downloading from official websites or the aforementioned platforms, make it a habit to read the reviews of the app. The feedback shared by genuine users will let you know if the app is trustworthy or not.6) Ensure the device is fully updated to the latest version of the operating system. Smartphone, tablet and computer makers regularly send security patches along with OS updates to protect your device from such cyber threats.7) Also, to be on the safe side, install anti-virus apps by renowned publishers such as Kaspersky, ESET and others.In India, if you fall victim to an online fraud, immediately call toll-free 1930. It is run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, and once you share the bank transaction details, they will be able to trace and freeze the mule bank accounts. sources.headline: SBI customers’ data leak: Here’s how to protect yourself from phishing attacks

brief_bullets: A significant data breach at the State Bank of India has exposed sensitive customer information, including mobile numbers, residential addresses, and unique CIF identifiers, which are currently being auctioned on the darknet. While initial reports suggest approximately 4,000 accounts were compromised, the scope of the exposure potentially threatens a much larger user base. Malicious actors are leveraging this personally identifiable information to conduct sophisticated phishing campaigns and digital arrest scams by impersonating law enforcement or bank officials. In response, cybersecurity experts are urging customers to immediately update credentials, avoid suspicious links, and verify all official communications through authorized bank channels to mitigate the heightened risk of financial fraud and identity theft.
why_it_matters_bullets: This breach undermines public trust in digital banking and necessitates urgent, widespread adoption of advanced multi-factor authentication protocols.
